newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwanese not so bullish in Year of the Bull.
newsitem.headline: Taiwanese not so bullish in Year of the Bull.

text.p: People in Taiwan are sceptical about prospects in 1997, the Year of the Bull in the lunar calendar, saying they are more pessimistic about the island's future and relations with China, a poll said on Wednesday.
The opinion poll, conducted by the mass-circulation China Times, showed that 20 percent of 969 respondents believed relations between Taiwan and China would deteriorate in 1997.
A similar survey conducted at the end of 1995 showed only 7.9 percent thought Taiwan-China relations would worsen in 1996.

Taiwan and the Chinese mainland have been divided since 1949. Beijing regards the island as a renegade province that is not entitled to international recognition, and has stepped up pressure to bring the Nationalist-ruled island under the communist mainland's sovereignty.
Some 38 percent of people polled said Hong Kong's mid-1997 handover to China from Britain would have a negative impact on Taiwan's political future.

The poll corresponded with recent surveys that showed Taiwan still distrusts China and that Beijing's handling of Hong Kong's handover has made Taiwanese wary of their own future in view of China's vow to return Taiwan to the motherland.
Taipei espouses eventual reunification but says it cannot consider the issue until China adopts democratic reforms like those in Taiwan.
Only 13.8 percent of Taiwan's people said they wished to reunify with China, while 14.3 percent supported Taiwan's independence. A total of 54.4 percent said they preferred the status quo.
An increasing number of people said the island's drive to boost its international profile would be futile.
Twenty-nine percent said Taiwan's international status would worsen in 1997, a dramatic increase from two percent a year ago.
Some 32 percent were pessimistic about Taiwan's "Asian dragon" economy in 1997 despite the government's optimistic outlook.
